inventor.match: Match each toy to its inventor.

rows.label: Kewpie doll
rows.hook: began as a cherubic comic-strip character that became a widely collected figurine

rows.label: LEGO
rows.hook: gave generations of children interlocking plastic bricks that snap together to build almost anything

rows.label: Scrabble
rows.hook: challenges players to form words on a grid using lettered tiles worth different point values

rows.label: Barbie
rows.description: fashion doll brand and media franchise
rows.hook: became the best-known fashion doll in the world, sparking endless outfits, careers, and dream houses

rows.label: Rubik's Cube
rows.description: 3-D combination puzzle with many different permutations
rows.hook: is a twisting puzzle with colored squares that must be lined up to match on every side

rows.label: Tamagotchi
rows.hook: was a pocket-sized digital pet that had to be fed and cared for or it would virtually die

rows.label: Yahtzee
rows.hook: challenges players to roll five dice into matching combinations for points

rows.label: Beanie Baby
rows.hook: turned small stuffed animals into a collecting craze built on hard-to-find limited editions

rows.label: Raggedy Ann
rows.hook: is a floppy, red-haired rag doll from a series of classic children's books

rows.label: Bratz
rows.description: American production line of fashion dolls and merchandise
rows.hook: brought a line of stylish, big-eyed fashion dolls with an edgier look than traditional dolls

rows.label: Furby
rows.hook: was a furry robotic toy that seemed to learn words and react to how it was treated

rows.label: Jenga
rows.description: game played with tower of blocks
rows.hook: is a stacking game where players pull wooden blocks from a tower without making it fall
